_comment: How a person's words become a corpus lookup. Keys are lowercase, punctuation stripped. Each entry narrows a query to a vendor, a product, a product_class, or some combination. query.py also does substring matching against vendor and product names, so this file only needs the terms that substring matching would miss: abbreviations, slang, model numbers and product names that changed.
_ambiguous_comment: Product aliases whose ordinary meaning competes with the product name. resolve() will not let one of these resolve on its own: the owning vendor has to appear within two tokens of it. Without that gate a caller asking about "runtime application self-protection" resolved to Android Runtime and Cisco IOS and was told RESOLUTION: product, with a GeoServer deserialisation record at rank 1 -- reported by a consuming content-pack session. The list is curated rather than derived, because both derivations tried are candidate generators and neither is a decider. Counting records whose vendor differs but whose prose carries the word ranks platform 85, client 31, tools 25, firewall 25 -- useful -- but also windows 17 and microsoft 11, which are not ambiguous to a caller who types them, while runtime and ios score 7 each and would sit far down the list. /usr/share/dict/words is worse: it flags confluence, chromium, outlook, asa and tomcat, and contains neither runtime nor ios. Add an entry when a caller could plausibly write the word meaning something other than the product.
_rasp_comment: Mobile application shielding and RASP. These thirteen vendors are refused as sources, measured: zero files across 1,347 upstream packs, and a shielded binary's attestation goes to the vendor's own SaaS rather than a tenant dataset, so there is no evidence_type for it. That refusal stands and none of it is re-read. What these aliases do is different: they route the question to the classes a build-integrated SDK behaves as, so a caller who names one gets a labelled CLASS-LEVEL answer about compiling a third-party binary-rewriting dependency into a pipeline, instead of exit 1 -- or, before 0.29.0, an Android Runtime and a GeoServer record. dev.library and app.cicd reach 59 findings, 48 of them SUPPLY. security.edr fills two more loci and is deliberately not here: it derives ENDPOINT, and the handset is the one plane this corpus declines to advise on, which is the mistake this corpus made once with app.mdm and corrected. ENDPOINT and ORGANISATION come back as LOCUS_ABSENT, which is the honest answer and not a gap to paper over. Licel joined them 2026-09-04 on its own measurement rather than by resemblance: zero files for licel and dexprotector across 1,350 upstream packs, the same result the thirteen returned. It was reported by a consuming content-pack session, whose Licel Alice question returned nothing while Guardsquare answered -- the route existed and the vendor was simply missing from it, which is a registration gap and not a corpus gap. Licel's other product, Alice, is a real product name and an ordinary given name, so it is NOT here: it sits in product_aliases under the ambiguous gate, resolving only within two tokens of licel. class_aliases has no gate, which is why a word like that cannot live in this table. Four aliases are known to still resolve falsely and are kept rather than deleted: ran, relay, ad and switch. Only switch is the sole route to its class; identity.directory, telecom.ran and ot.protection_relay each keep three or more unambiguous aliases, so deleting ad, ran or relay would cost no class coverage. Measured 2026-09-13; the earlier claim that each was the only way into its class was wrong.

ambiguous_aliases.alice: an ordinary given name; Licel ships a product called Alice
ambiguous_aliases.beacon: a C2 beacon, the thing this corpus is mostly about
ambiguous_aliases.cargo: Rust's package manager, and the English word
ambiguous_aliases.client: any client, in almost every record here
ambiguous_aliases.device management: the concept; the class_aliases entry already carries app.mdm and app.rmm
ambiguous_aliases.web server: the concept, and the class; the alias points at a backup product
ambiguous_aliases.multiple products: a phrase an advisory uses, not a product
ambiguous_aliases.controllers: any controller, including every OT one
ambiguous_aliases.core: a core, a kernel, a product edition
ambiguous_aliases.defender: the defender, who is the reader of every finding here
ambiguous_aliases.director: a person, and a dozen products
ambiguous_aliases.edge: the network edge, an edge device
ambiguous_aliases.enterprise: the edition suffix on half the software here
ambiguous_aliases.firewall: the class, which is what a caller means by it
ambiguous_aliases.ics: industrial control systems, which is the ot.ics class
ambiguous_aliases.ios: Apple iOS, far more often than Cisco IOS
ambiguous_aliases.office: a physical office, an office network
ambiguous_aliases.publisher: the publisher of a source, a word this corpus uses constantly in prose
ambiguous_aliases.routers: the class, which is what a caller means by it
ambiguous_aliases.runtime: any runtime, and the word in "runtime protection"
ambiguous_aliases.spring: the season, and the English word
ambiguous_aliases.word: the English word, the most generic token in the table
